basic_information.short_title: Creation of the Municipality of Sheik Abas Hamza
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE MUNICIPALITY OF SHEIK ABAS HAMZA IN THE PROVINCE OF MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Carves 10 barangays out of the Municipality of Datu Odin Sinsuat to create a new municipality, Sheik Abas Hamza, in Maguindanao del Norte — subject to a plebiscite of the voters living there.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The Organic Law empowers the Bangsamoro Government to create, divide, merge or abolish municipalities and barangays by act of Parliament, provided the change is ratified by the people directly affected.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: If ratified, 10 barangays covering about 164.4 square kilometres become a distinct and independent municipality with its own appointed mayor, vice-mayor and eight-member council, seated at Barangay Bugawas.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of the 10 barangays, who vote in the plebiscite
Residents of the remaining parts of Datu Odin Sinsuat, the mother municipality
Taxpayers, since ₱2.5 million a month is provided until the new municipality gets its revenue share
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: The act is in force, but corporate existence depends on ratification in a plebiscite to be held within 60 days of approval.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: You decide. This act creates the Municipality of Sheik Abas Hamza out of 10 barangays of Datu Odin Sinsuat — but only if a majority of voters there approve it in a plebiscite.
in_practice: 10 barangays separate from Datu Odin Sinsuat: Labungan, Taviran, Baka, Sapalan, Sifaran, Bugawas, Bitu, Kurintem, Margues and Makir
Land area of 164,387,474 square metres — about 164.4 square kilometres
The seat of government is Barangay Bugawas, renamed the Poblacion
A plebiscite of qualified voters decides it, within 60 days of approval, run by COMELEC
Plebiscite costs come from the BARMM Contingent Fund under the FY2024 budget
The Chief Minister appoints the first mayor, vice-mayor and eight Sangguniang Bayan members
₱2,500,000 a month until the municipality receives its Internal Revenue Allotment share

for_specific_groups.Voters in the 10 barangays: Your vote creates the municipality — it does not exist until a majority of votes cast ratifies it.
for_specific_groups.Residents of the rest of Datu Odin Sinsu: The mother municipality loses 10 barangays if the plebiscite passes.
for_specific_groups.Incumbent Sangguniang Bayan members of D: If you actually reside in the new municipality, you serve out your remaining term in the mother municipality.
for_specific_groups.Anyone expecting to elect the first offi: The first mayor, vice-mayor and council are appointed by the Chief Minister until the next regular election.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Maguindanao del Norte — 10 barangays currently in Datu Odin Sinsuat.
what_you_can_do: Check whether your barangay is among the 10 named in Section 2
Ask COMELEC when it is scheduled; the act set 60 days from approval
watch_out_for: The first set of municipal officials is appointed, not elected.
Financial assistance is a floor — 'not less than' ₱2.5 million monthly — with no ceiling stated.
The act states a land area but no population figure.
The plebiscite cost depends on the FY2024 Contingent Fund.

key_terms_explained.Plebiscite: A vote of the people directly affected, required before a municipality can be created.
key_terms_explained.Poblacion: The seat of government of a municipality — here, Barangay Bugawas.
key_terms_explained.IRA / Internal Revenue Allotment: A local government's share of national taxes.
key_terms_explained.Mother municipality: The municipality the new one is carved out of — here, Datu Odin Sinsuat.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Akhirah 07, 1445 / 20 December 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 26 December 2023.

benefits.headline: A new municipality of 10 barangays and about 164 square kilometres, with ₱2.5 million a month until its tax share arrives.

direct_benefits.benefit: A local government seated in your own area
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Subject to ratification in the plebiscite

direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The new Municipal Government of Sheik Abas Hamza
direct_benefits.amount: Not less than ₱2.5 million every month until the IRA share is allocated

indirect_benefits: Entitlement to a share of national taxes once allocated
Services delivered from a nearer seat of government
limitations: Nothing takes effect without a favourable plebiscite.
The first officials are appointed, not elected.

for_citizens: None beyond voting in the plebiscite, which is a right rather than a duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections (COMELEC), which conducts and supervises the plebiscite
where_to_complain.oversight: Office of the Chief Minister, which appoints the first municipal officials
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A resident of Barangay Taviran votes in the plebiscite. If a majority of votes cast approve, Taviran leaves Datu Odin Sinsuat for the new municipality.
A sitting councillor of Datu Odin Sinsuat who lives in Bugawas finishes their term serving the mother municipality.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Government may create, divide, merge, abolish or substantially alter the boundaries of municipalities or barangays by act of Parliament, with units so created entitled to their share in national taxes, provided the change is approved by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite in the political units directly affected.

Section 2 — Separates the barangays of Labungan, Taviran, Baka, Sapalan, Sifaran, Bugawas, Bitu, Kurintem, Margues and Makir from the Municipality of Datu Odin Sinsuat and constitutes them into the distinct and independent Municipality of Sheik Abas Hamza.
Section 3 — The seat of government is Barangay Bugawas, known hereafter as the Poblacion.
Section 4 — The municipality contains a land area of 164,387,474 square metres, and its territorial boundary follows the existing boundaries of the constituent barangays.

Section 5 — The municipality acquires corporate existence on ratification by a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters in a plebiscite in those barangays, to be held within 60 days after approval of the act. The Commission on Elections conducts and supervises it, with the cost taken from the BARMM Contingent Fund under the FY2024 appropriations.

Section 6 — The municipal government comprises a mayor, a vice-mayor and eight Sangguniang Bayan members appointed by the Chief Minister immediately after ratification, holding office until successors are elected at the next regular election. Incumbent elective Sangguniang Bayan members of Datu Odin Sinsuat who actually reside in the new municipality serve out their remaining terms in the mother municipality.

Section 7 — The Bangsamoro Government shall appropriate financial assistance of not less than ₱2,500,000 every month for the administration and operation of the Municipal Government of Sheik Abas Hamza until it is allocated its share in the Internal Revenue Allotment.
Section 10 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: The new Municipal Government of Sheik Abas Hamza
impact.allocated_budget: Not less than ₱2,500,000 per month until the municipality receives its Internal Revenue Allotment share; plebiscite costs from the BARMM Contingent Fund under FY2024.
impact.figures_note: Quoted from Sections 4, 5 and 7. Land area 164,387,474 square metres; no population figure is stated.

related_legislation.related_note: Passed the same day as BAA 53 (Nuling) and BAA 54 (Datu Sinsuat Balabaran). Section 5, the plebiscite requirement, was later amended by BAA 71.

implementation_status.budget_appropriated: Not less than ₱2,500,000 monthly, pending IRA allocation
implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. Section 5 was subsequently amended by BAA 71 — read that act for the plebiscite requirement as it now stands.

citizen_questions.q: Does this create the municipality straight away?
citizen_questions.a: No. Corporate existence depends on ratification by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite of the affected barangays. Note that Section 5 was later amended by BAA 71.
Ten, currently in Datu Odin Sinsuat: Labungan, Taviran, Baka, Sapalan, Sifaran, Bugawas, Bitu, Kurintem, Margues and Makir.
164,387,474 square metres — roughly 164 square kilometres. The act gives no population figure.

citizen_questions.q: Who will be the first mayor?
citizen_questions.a: Whoever the Chief Minister appoints. The first mayor, vice-mayor and eight councillors are appointed after ratification and serve until the next regular election.

citizen_questions.q: How will it pay for itself?
citizen_questions.a: Not less than ₱2.5 million a month from the Bangsamoro Government until it receives its Internal Revenue Allotment share.
